Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up and latency/throughput requirements

Neha / team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful discussion. Quick recap from our side and a few outstanding questions so we can decide whether to go Hosted API or Dedicated capacity for our inference traffic.

Requirements recap:
- Model: proprietary scoring model (13B) with persistent KV cache per session
- Latency target: p95 < 100ms for single-turn scoring
- Steady throughput: ~100-130 req/s (production)
- Daily short bursts: up to ~200 req/s for 5-10 minutes during peak batch windows
- Data: non-sensitive transactional data (not PHI/PII) but must remain in US region

Questions:
1) Given the p95 and steady qps, is Hosted API sufficient or do we need Dedicated to guarantee latency?
2) How do you handle short bursts — autoscaling vs burst capacity on Dedicated?
3) Rough lead time and order-of-magnitude cost difference for Dedicated reserved capacity vs Hosted at our qps?

Attaching our internal traffic heatmap (short excel) — happy to provide more telemetry if helpful.

Next steps: please advise recommended path and proposed next call (technical deep-dive + provisioning planning).

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds

Hi Tom — great to meet you and thanks for the clear recap. Replied inline with recommendations and next steps.

Short answer: based on the p95 <100ms requirement and steady 100-130 req/s with short 200 req/s bursts, Dedicated capacity is the safer recommendation for predictable latency SLOs. Hosted API can work for many customers, but for sub-100ms p95 at that sustained qps (with KV cache needs) you’ll generally see more consistent results on Dedicated where we can reserve GPU pools and tune batching/cache behavior.

Key notes:
- Latency: Dedicated lets us pin a model variant and control batching windows more tightly (lower variability). For your model size + KV cache, we can avoid multi-tenant noisy neighbor effects.
- Throughput & bursts: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and short burst capacity. We typically recommend configuring a small headroom (20-50%) and using our burst queue to cover the 5-10m spikes; also we can run a short load test to validate burst behavior.
- Lead time: Dedicated provisioning estimate ~3-4 weeks for reserved capacity (depends on region availability).
- Cost: order-of-magnitude: Dedicated reserved capacity with a monthly commit will usually be ~2-3x cheaper per token vs on-demand Hosted at sustained qps (ballpark depends on model and quantization). We’ll give a tailored estimate after we see telemetry.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with Dylan to review traffic patterns, KV cache usage, and the model binary — 60m session.
2) Short POC: 2-week Dedicated trial with load test and latency report.
3) Share Mutual Action Plan and a first-pass SLA/pricing draft.

I attached a short matrix that compares Hosted vs Dedicated for latency/throughput tradeoffs. I’ll loop Dylan to schedule the deep-dive — are mornings (PST) better for you this week?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
